subtopic: A conflict between two team members
subtype: Approach: emotion-aware timing of the discussion [Thinking]
passage: Note from Uday, engineering director. On Monday Manjula stopped by my desk. Two of her people, Tanmay and Divya, had been snapping at each other all week. Manjula wanted to sort it out, but said, "They're both running on empty until Thursday's launch. If I bring it up now, it lands as one more problem." So she waited. The launch went out on Thursday evening. On Friday afternoon Manjula took the two of them to a quiet corner with coffee. I walked past twice: voices low, and at one point a laugh. By Monday Manjula told me they had agreed who reviews what. All I did was leave them alone and approve a half-day for the team.

qa.q: When did Manjula meet Tanmay and Divya to talk?
qa.a: Manjula took them to a quiet corner on Friday afternoon.

qa.q: Why did Manjula wait before raising the problem, and what was she worried about?
qa.a: Manjula worried that Tanmay and Divya were too exhausted before launch, and that raising it then would feel like one more problem.

qa.q: What else could Manjula do to keep the peace, and why?
qa.a: Manjula could check in with each of them a week later, because a calm talk may still need a follow-up to settle into habit.

qa.q: How might Divya have felt about the timing of the talk?
qa.a: Divya probably felt relieved and more open, since the pressure of the launch was over and there was space to speak calmly.

grounding: Illustrates a lead seeing that two colleagues are stressed by a release and waiting until the day after launch to talk, when the discussion is calm.
